models_evaluated: Croce post-traumatic VAP prediction model (logistic regression)

links.outcome: Discrimination and calibration of externally developed model on local historical data before and after recalibration
links.effect: Original AUC 0.83, mean predicted risk 6.4% vs observed 10.6%, calibration slope 0.63; after full recalibration AUC 0.84, Brier 0.087, calibration improved.
links.quote: After full model recalibration, discrimination (AUC 0.84, 95% CI 0.80-0.88) and calibration improved.

links.outcome: Calibration and discrimination after local intercept and full recalibration of imported model
links.effect: Intercept moved from -3.08 to 0.80, giving better calibration; full recalibration AUC 0.84 and Brier 0.089 to 0.087; adding age raised AUC to 0.87.
links.quote: After intercept recalibration, the model’s intercept increased from -3.08 in the Croce model to 0.80 in our cohort, showing better calibration (Fig. 2 B).

links.outcome: Differences between development and local cohorts and resulting miscalibration
links.effect: Croce cohort had more penetrating trauma (23% vs 3%), younger patients (median 35 vs 51), more laparotomy (14% vs 3%); pneumonia incidence 5.6% vs 10.6%; calibration slope 0.63.
links.quote: However, in Croce’s cohort, the incidence of penetrating trauma was higher (23% vs. 3%), patients were younger (median 35 vs. 51 years), and relatively more patients underwent an emergent laparotomy (14% vs. 3%) compared to the Dutch cohort [ 6 ].

links.outcome: Model performance at a new external site relative to development
links.effect: AUC fell from 0.97 at internal validation to 0.83 externally; predicted risk too low (6.4% vs 10.6%); calibration slope 0.63.
links.quote: The original model showed good discriminatory capacity (AUC 0.83, 95% CI 0.79 – 0.87) but was overfitted for use in the Dutch population (calibration slope 0.63; mean predicted risk 6.4% vs. 10.6% observed risk).

links.outcome: Generalization of predictive model to a new population and outcome definition
links.effect: Model developed for VAP in a US center underpredicted nosocomial pneumonia in a Dutch cohort; calibration slope 0.63.
links.quote: The calibration slope was 0.63, suggesting some overfitting in the original study compared to our population.

links.outcome: Applicability of original risk cutoff to local population after recalibration
links.effect: Original 0.5 cutoff not workable; few recalibrated predicted probabilities above 0.25.
links.quote: A comparable cutoff is not yet reasonable for Dutch level-1 trauma patients when using the recalibrated or updated model.

models_evaluated: Croce post-traumatic ventilator-associated pneumonia prediction model
Croce model without mechanism of injury

links.outcome: External validation performance
links.effect: External validation showed AUC 0.83 (95% CI 0.79 – 0.87), calibration slope 0.63, and underprediction: mean predicted risk 6.4% vs. 10.6% observed.
links.quote: The original model showed good discriminatory capacity (AUC 0.83, 95% CI 0.79 – 0.87) but was overfitted for use in the Dutch population (calibration slope 0.63; mean predicted risk 6.4% vs. 10.6% observed risk).

links.outcome: Discrimination-calibration mismatch
links.effect: Despite AUC 0.83 (95% CI 0.79 – 0.87), calibration was poor: slope 0.63 and mean predicted risk 6.4% vs. 10.6% observed.
links.quote: The original model showed good discriminatory capacity (AUC 0.83, 95% CI 0.79 – 0.87) but was overfitted for use in the Dutch population (calibration slope 0.63; mean predicted risk 6.4% vs. 10.6% observed risk).

links.outcome: Local validation performance
links.effect: On local Dutch historical data, AUC was 0.83 (95% CI 0.79 – 0.87), calibration slope 0.63, and predicted risk 6.4% vs. 10.6% observed.
links.quote: The original model showed good discriminatory capacity (AUC 0.83, 95% CI 0.79 – 0.87) but was overfitted for use in the Dutch population (calibration slope 0.63; mean predicted risk 6.4% vs. 10.6% observed risk).

links.outcome: Development-local population shift
links.effect: Compared with Dutch cohort, Croce cohort had more penetrating trauma (23% vs. 3%), younger age (median 35 vs. 51), and more emergent laparotomy (14% vs. 3%).
links.quote: However, in Croce’s cohort, the incidence of penetrating trauma was higher (23% vs. 3%), patients were younger (median 35 vs. 51 years), and relatively more patients underwent an emergent laparotomy (14% vs. 3%) compared to the Dutch cohort [ 6 ].

links.outcome: Local recalibration performance
links.effect: Full recalibration improved AUC to 0.84 (95% CI 0.80 – 0.88) with better calibration; Brier’s statistic improved to 0.087.
links.quote: The first model recalibration slightly improved the discriminatory capacity (AUC 0.84, 95% CI 0.80 – 0.88) and showed an overall better concordance in calibration (Fig. 3 ).

links.outcome: discrimination and calibration of external prediction model
links.effect: External validation showed AUC of 0.83 (95% CI 0.79-0.87), mean predicted risk 6.4% versus 10.6% observed risk, and calibration slope 0.63, reflecting overfitting compared to internal validation AUC of 0.97.
links.quote: The original model showed good discriminatory capacity (AUC 0.83, 95% CI 0.79 – 0.87) but was overfitted for use in the Dutch population (calibration slope 0.63; mean predicted risk 6.4% vs. 10.6% observed risk).

links.outcome: discrimination and calibration after local model recalibration
links.effect: Full recalibration improved discriminatory capacity to AUC 0.84 (95% CI 0.80-0.88), improved calibration concordance, and Brier statistic improved from 0.089 to 0.087.
links.quote: Full recalibration of the model improved the discriminatory capacity (AUC 0.84, 95% CI 0.80 – 0.88) and calibration in our study cohort.

screen.practice: local validation and recalibration before deployment
screen.reason: The study evaluates the external validation and local recalibration of an existing predictive risk model (Croce's model) on a new hospital cohort, comparing performance before and after recalibration.
